stack_arguments.name: receiver_candidate_word
stack_arguments.zero_behavior: load [ECX+0x150] and use that value as the tail-call ECX receiver candidate
stack_arguments.nonzero_behavior: use the incoming value directly as the tail-call ECX receiver candidate; no uint32 selector semantics are established

type_dependencies: OpaqueEditor for ECX; the mode-manager caller passes this+0x5c, while Editor_Save passes its own this
A nonzero incoming stack word becomes the tail-call ECX receiver candidate directly; no uint32 selector semantics are established
A zero incoming stack word instead loads [ECX+0x150], whose opaque value becomes the tail-call ECX receiver candidate
The result retains pointer-like status and is used only through a null/nonzero guard by 0x005dda30; no boolean return is inferred

evidence.fact: The function receives OpaqueEditor in ECX and reads one unclassified 32-bit stack word. A zero word causes [ECX+0x150] to be loaded as the receiver candidate and returns zero only when that load is null; a nonzero word skips the +0x150 load.

For the nonzero path, the incoming stack word itself is moved to ECX as the tail-call receiver candidate; for the zero path, [ECX+0x150] is moved there instead. Both paths rewrite the outgoing stack word to 1 and tail-jump to 0x004c49e0. The incoming nonzero value is not established as a uint32 selector.

The mode-manager call at 0x005dda42 loads manager+0x5c into ECX and passes stack value 0. Editor_Save calls 0x00574a20 at 0x0057775a with ECX=Editor_Save this and [Editor_Save this+0x154] on the stack, exercising the direct nonzero receiver-candidate path when nonzero.
0x00574a20 normalizes the outgoing stack word to 1 before the tail call, so the helper takes its 0x1c branch and returns the receiver candidate's +0x1c word.
